record.original_question: Determine all minor-minimal graphs that do not embed in the torus.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2 Find the minor-minimal non-toroidal graphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graph $H$ is called a minor of a graph $G$ if $H$ can be obtained from a subgraph of $G$ by contracting edges. A graph $G$ is said to embed in the torus if it can be drawn on the torus (the orientable surface of genus 1) without edge crossings; otherwise $G$ is called non-toroidal. A graph $G$ is a minor-minimal non-toroidal graph (equivalently, a forbidden minor for toroidal embeddability) if $G$ does not embed in the torus, but every proper minor of $G$ does.

By the Robertson–Seymour theorem, the set $\mathcal{H}$ of all minor-minimal non-toroidal graphs (up to isomorphism) is finite. Determine $\mathcal{H}$ explicitly: produce a complete and finite list of all minor-minimal graphs that do not embed in the torus.
artifact.status_search_result: The complete set of forbidden minors for embeddability in the torus is known to be finite by the Robertson–Seymour theorem but has not been determined. Computer searches have produced large lower bounds (at least 17,000+ minor-minimal non-toroidal graphs are known), and partial results exist for restricted families (e.g., graphs without a $K_{3,3}$-minor, or of low connectivity), but the full list remains unknown.

status_evidence.title: Toroidal graph - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: the complete set H is not known, but it has at least 17,523 graphs
status_evidence.claim: Complete list of toroidal forbidden minors is unknown; only lower bounds exist.

status_evidence.title: Robertson–Seymour theorem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: it tells us that the set of toroidal graphs has a finite obstruction set, but it does not provide any such set
status_evidence.claim: The theorem guarantees finiteness but does not yield the explicit obstruction set for the torus.

status_evidence.title: Forbidden Minors: Finding the Finite Few
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of known forbidden minor sets including partial progress on toroidal obstructions
status_evidence.claim: The toroidal obstruction set is a well-known open problem with only partial enumerations.
